subject: Plumery - sudden SLA violations after model patch (v4.2-q)
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@plumery.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Plumery Support <support@plumery.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production spike: 5xx and p99 soar after model patch v4.2-q

Hi Soojin,

We pushed your v4.2-q model patch to canary at 07:40 PT and promoted to prod at 08:30 PT (traffic split 100%). Within about 20 minutes we saw:

- 5xx rate jump from ~0.2% to 4.7%
- p95/p99 latency go from 220ms/410ms to 1.1s/2.6s
- throughput drop ~18% (requests/sec) despite same traffic

Attached are a short tail of decoder errors and a throughput plot. We also have a HubSpot ticket open: PLUM-4821.

Can your team roll this back? Our users are seeing failures and timeouts. We need an ETA and a mitigation (rate-limit or rollback).

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Site Reliability
Plumery, Inc.

Attachments: error_snapshot.log (text), throughput_plot.png (image)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production spike: 5xx and p99 soar after model patch v4.2-q

Hi Evan — I see the ticket and logs, thanks for the quick flag.

We've looped in Priya (AM) for customer coordination and Irene (SRE) to investigate the runtime profile. Irene — can you confirm whether this is a model variant/quant mismatch or an infra kernel issue?

Short term: we can revert to the previous model variant (v4.1-std) within 20 minutes if you want us to do that now. If you prefer we can throttle calls and keep the variant until we understand root cause.

Evan, please confirm rollback or throttle preference. We'll stand by and prepare a rollback plan.

— Soojin

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@plumery.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 5xx and p99 soar after model patch v4.2-q

Quick triage from runtime: we see an increased number of decoder OOM/probe timeouts and significantly longer per-token decode in the v4.2-q variant. Early indicators point to a quantization profile change shipped with v4.2-q — kernels falling back to slower code paths for longer sequences. Evidence: stack traces in error_snapshot.log, and a diff between active quant metadata (attached initial-diff.txt).

Initial mitigation options (ranked):
1) Immediate rollback to v4.1-std (fastest, low-risk) — ETA: ~15-20 minutes to complete and validate routing.
2) Apply temporary request throttling/traffic shaping to reduce concurrency and relieve backpressure — ETA: ~10 minutes to configure on client side but needs Redis token bucket config on our side to be adjusted.
3) Patch quant profile (risky, longer) — ETA: several hours, requires kernel selection and QA.

I'm recommending rollback for now so Plumery's users are stable; we can then run a controlled canary with the updated quant profile after additional kernel tuning.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-diff.txt (text) — quant metadata diff
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@plumery.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Plumery production SLA violations after v4.2-q - exec heads up

Vivek — looping you in. Plumery (high-touch enterprise) experienced a sharp p99/5xx spike immediately following deployment of v4.2-q (quantized variant). Irene's triage points to a quant profile -> slow-path kernel fallback on longer sequences.

Planned immediate action: rollback to v4.1-std (Irene ETA 15-20m) and then a hotfix cadence:
- rollback and validation (T+20m)
- post-rollback perf check (T+40m)
- follow-up RCA + PM: full kernel selection pass and tighter canary gates before any qprofile variants (48–72h)

Customer asks: credit for downtime window and a firm timeline for a safe re-rollout. I recommend we approve a small service credit and prioritize kernel tuning for this customer. Priya — please start the credit request workflow and log with PLUM-4821.

Evan — can you confirm the rollback window is acceptable? Also: please attach two representative request IDs so we can trace decode paths.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Escalation: Plumery production SLA violations after v4.2-q - exec heads up

Thanks everyone — rollback completed at 10:38 PT and we saw p99/p95 and 5xx fall back to baseline by ~10:50 PT. Throughput returned to normal by 11:05 PT. Attaching a post-rollback snippet; happy to share more logs.

We appreciate the quick response and the offer to open a credit. We'll want a short postmortem and a plan for safer qprofile rollouts.

Evan Brooks
Site Reliability
Plumery, Inc.
